name: Make-Up
label: Dischord
lede: Nation of Ulysses was a political party; its successor was a church. Five years, matching suits, a congregation instead of an audience, and a plan to quit the minute everybody started copying them.

eras.title: The party dissolves, the church opens
eras.text: Nation of Ulysses had ended in 1992 with its doctrine intact. Ian Svenonius, James Canty and Steve Gamboa regrouped, brought in bassist Michelle Mae from Olympia, and swapped the manifesto for the form of a gospel service: call, response, and the audience as a fifth member.

years.h: Before Make-Up: Cupid Car Club, M.P.
years.p: [[Ian Svenonius|0ef9be87-0dbe-4551-a526-f3f6891a2e9d]], [[James Canty|ffc732f4-15a3-42e1-a498-965c1d793e35]] and Steve Gamboa play in the short-lived Cupid Car Club, M.P., which leaves one 7", Werewolves, on Kill Rock Stars.

q: Our music is gospel-based. It's rhythm-based, with a subverted guitar.
years.p: Ian Svenonius sings, James Canty plays guitar and organ, Steve Gamboa moves from bass to drums, and [[Michelle Mae|ed4db6af-9894-4ad8-a381-ec9cddfd7544]] joins on bass from Olympia's [[The Frumpies|02231403-76b1-4a4c-accc-714eda94566f]]. Dischord dates Make-Up's start to February 1995.
years.xp:
Dischord's bio describes Make-Up as a group that plays superior, original music with the freneticism, catharsis and spirituality of gospel. Svenonius put the difference from Nation of Ulysses simply: that band was a political party, this one was based on gospel.

They called the sound gospel yeh-yeh, borrowing gospel's form rather than its content and pairing it with the bubblegum gloss of French yé-yé. The matching outfits were part of the program, meant to erase the individual rock star.

years.h: Debut single Blue Is Beautiful on Make-Up's own Black Gemini label
years.p: Make-Up's first 7" comes out on its own label, followed the same year by Trans-Pleasant Express, a split with [[Slant 6|ffe8acdb-3fa3-4f7e-8939-c3862138502d]] and R.U.A. Believer on K Records.

years.h: Destination: Love; Live! At Cold Rice · Dischord No. 99
years.p: A studio record dressed up as a live one, crowd noise and all, recorded in September 1995 on the Pirate "Mobile" with [[Guy Picciotto|f8200cea-b5e9-4145-b5a5-1d0838f2c288]] of [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]] producing. Dischord calls it Make-Up's debut full-length.

eras.title: Free Arthur Lee
eras.text: Make-Up worked fast: singles on four labels, the London live album After Dark, and the K Records LP Sound Verite produced by Calvin Johnson. The politics never left, they just got a better rhythm section.

years.p: Make-Up's second single on Time Bomb, which had also released We're Having a Baby in 1995.

years.h: A live set in London becomes After Dark
years.p: Make-Up record a live set in London. [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] mixes it at Inner Ear, and it comes out as After Dark, Dischord No. 105, in February 1997.

[[Calvin Johnson|cac7a688-14a8-46c3-8fc8-11cca866677c]] produces Make-Up's LP for Olympia's K Records, one month after After Dark. The band also lands on K's Selector Dub Narcotic compilation that year.
Make-Up's single for Love singer Arthur Lee, jailed in 1996 after firing a gun during a dispute with a neighbor and for illegal firearms possession. Lee was released in 2001.

years.h: Wade in the Water 7" on All City
years.p: Make-Up cover the traditional spiritual "Wade in the Water" for a single on All City Records.

eras.title: Pow! To the people
eras.text: Make-Up's records got stranger and better. Royal Trux produced In Mass Mind, Pitchfork compared Save Yourself to the Rolling Stones, and filmmaker James Schneider turned the band into a thirty-two-minute movie.

years.p: Make-Up's second Dischord LP, fourteen tracks, recorded at Stillness Studio and produced by Neil Hagerty and Jennifer Herrema of [[Royal Trux|87e27246-8c40-407f-bfb3-5dc416557eeb]]. The vinyl was pressed on pink wax.

years.cap: Blue Is Beautiful, dir. James Schneider
years.h: Blue Is Beautiful: James Schneider's film of Make-Up
years.p: Dischord No. 114 is a VHS: Blue Is Beautiful, a 32-minute film about Make-Up by James Schneider. It later resurfaces on the In Film/On Video DVD.

years.h: Singles U R My Intended and Pow! To the People
years.p: Make-Up release two 1998 singles, one on K and one on Southern, plus a split 7" with Scottish band Lungleg.
K Records gathers Make-Up's scattered 7"s and B-sides onto one album.
Make-Up's final studio album, on K Records. Pitchfork said it could stand next to the Rolling Stones' Between the Buttons.
Alex Minoff, later of Golden and [[Extra Golden|c39b100f-0e43-4e39-b244-a33d6dcb09a0]], joins Make-Up as a fifth member for the band's final months.

eras.title: The five-year plan, completed
eras.text: Make-Up quit in 2000 while the uniforms still fit. Ian Svenonius's stated reason: too many copycat groups had taken the look and sound and emptied it out.

q: We had a five year plan like Stalin.
years.h: Make-Up break up, saying they've been copied
years.p: Make-Up dissolves, saying copycat groups had borrowed its look and sound for empty, counter-revolutionary ends.
years.xp:
Ian Svenonius framed the split as a plan fulfilled rather than a band falling apart: Make-Up's presentation had become redundant because it was being copied so much, so there was no need to keep doing it. Other people could carry it now.

What came next came fast. Svenonius, Michelle Mae and Alex Minoff formed [[Weird War|f6fb557c-2f0f-4d17-97d9-13371fbe0ea6]] (briefly renamed Scene Creamers) on Drag City. James Canty joined [[Ted Leo and the Pharmacists|31095622-5a1e-4f22-8ad1-b08eb6255f37]] and formed French Toast with Jerry Busher.

eras.title: The archive opens
eras.text: Six years after Make-Up ended, its live power finally got documented properly: the live album Untouchable Sound and the DVD In Film/On Video.

years.p: Drag City and Sea Note release a live Make-Up album from the band's last stretch, with Alex Minoff on guitar.
Dischord puts James Schneider's Make-Up film Blue Is Beautiful on DVD. Ian Svenonius also publishes The Psychic Soviet, a book of essays, through Drag City.

eras.title: A reunion nobody saw coming
eras.text: For a band that had made quitting part of the concept, Make-Up coming back in 2012 was its own kind of provocation. They did it anyway, and toured again in 2019.

years.h: Make-Up reunite at ATP's I'll Be Your Mirror, London
years.p: Make-Up's first show since 2000 is at All Tomorrow's Parties' I'll Be Your Mirror at London's Alexandra Palace, May 25–27, alongside Slayer playing Reign in Blood.
Dischord's 2009 remastered LP of Destination: Love; Live! At Cold Rice went out of print quickly, so Dischord reissued it again in June 2012.

years.h: Make-Up tour again, with Mark Cisneros on drums
years.p: Make-Up announce a 2019 reunion tour and a reissue of Save Yourself. On the later tours Mark Cisneros of [[Des Demonas|7536e54b-aa8f-429a-aa62-21184a53c14c]] and Kid Congo Powers' band plays drums in place of Steve Gamboa.
